alt: Five theme panels with their guiding principles and recommended topics: identities, experiences, human ingenuity, social organization and sharing the planet, each with topics such as lifestyles, migration, technology, education and the environment.
caption: Build vocabulary across all five themes, not just the ones you discussed most.

alt: A table comparing SL and HL. Paper 1 lasts 1 hour 15 minutes for 250 to 400 words at SL, and 1 hour 30 minutes for 450 to 600 words at HL. Listening is 45 minutes at SL and 1 hour at HL; reading is 1 hour at both. HL studies two literary works, so its oral stimulus is a literary excerpt rather than a visual image, with 20 rather than 15 minutes of preparation.
caption: Same themes and weightings, different durations, word ranges and oral stimulus.

alt: A bar of four equal 25% shares: Paper 1 writing, Paper 2 listening, Paper 2 reading and the individual oral, the same at SL and HL. Paper 2 together is 50%. Below, Paper 2 by raw marks: listening 25 and reading 40, so reading is nearly two-thirds of the raw marks.
caption: Equal weightings hide unequal raw marks: reading needs more practice.

alt: Three categories of text type with examples: personal (blog post, diary entry, email or letter to a friend), professional (formal letter, report, essay) and mass media (article, interview, speech). Paper 1 is marked on language, message and conceptual understanding, and the last penalises ignoring text type, register or audience.
caption: Format and register count alongside accurate language.
